handoff.purpose: Scan state derivation, acceptance parsing, and report dataclasses

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Pure derivation of architecture state from reach/switch reports; no writes, clock, or network per docstring

symbols.name: Acceptance
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for an acceptance record with validity and expiry checks

symbols.name: parse_acceptances
symbols.note: Parses raw acceptance list, marking malformed entries with problems, fail-closed

symbols.name: DriftItem
symbols.note: Dataclass for a drift finding with blocking property and dict serialization

symbols.name: DriftReport
symbols.note: Dataclass for a full drift report with blocking items and freshness metadata

claims.text: Pure: no writes, no clock, no network.
claims.why: The scan function only reads from injected reports and local computation; no filesystem writes, no time functions, no network calls are present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``reach_report`` and ``switch_report`` may be injected by a caller that already built them ... the page and the gate are then provably looking at the same analysis.
claims.why: The function checks `if reach_report is None` and `if switch_report is None` before calling the respective analyse functions, so injected reports are used as-is.

claims.text: ``index`` is only forwarded to reach for its structural cross-check.
claims.why: `index` is passed to `reach_mod.analyse(root, index=index)` and not used elsewhere in this chunk.

claims.text: The state also records WHICH TREE it was derived from (:func:`repo_state`). It belongs here rather than in the writer because it is a property of the scan ...
claims.why: `state` includes `"repo_state": repo_state(root, probe_dirty=probe_dirty)` which records the tree.

claims.text: TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically. Scoping it to islands meant a shim or an unknown whose only importer was a test could not be described that way at all.
claims.why: The code computes `unreached_facts` from `UNREACHED_CLASSES` (which includes more than islands) and then `test_only` from that set, so it is not scoped to islands.

claims.text: Two engines disagreeing about the import graph. reach REPORTS these and refuses to merge them ... the gate is where a disagreement that persists across a commit becomes somebody's problem.
claims.why: `index_extra_edges` is taken from `reach_report.index_extra_edges` and included in the state and sites; the gate logic is outside this chunk but the data is captured.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature. The feature it belongs to is documented and merely unconfigured -- ``daedalus doctor`` already reports it, and an architecture gate is a poor place to enumerate which secrets a machine is missing. ``secret`` is the switch engine's own classification, so this is a filter over one answer, not a second opinion about what a switch is.
claims.why: The code skips switches with `sw.kind == "secret"`, and filters out documented switches via `docs.documents(sw.name)`, matching the stated intent.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare ``continue``. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: The code builds `unparsable` from both `reach_report.unparsable` and `switch_report.unparsable`, and includes it in `counts`, `state`, and `sites`.

claims.text: The honest total: every module on disk that no entry point reaches, whatever reach called it. It is the number the page has to add up to, and it is what "islands=7" used to hide.
claims.why: `"unreached": len(islands) + len(unknown_mods) + len(shims)` sums all three classifications, as described.

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a ``problem``, and suppresses nothing. A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: Every entry, even malformed ones, is appended to `out` as an `Acceptance` with a `problem` string; nothing is dropped.

claims.text: ``today`` binds the horizon to the CALENDAR. Without it the only rule is ``until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS``, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now. Omitting ``today`` keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one ...
claims.why: The `d_since > today` check is guarded by `if d_since and today`, so omitting `today` skips only that check while horizon and date-shape checks still run.

claims.text: The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see :func:`snapshot_freshness`.
claims.why: The `snapshot_freshness` function is not in this chunk, so the claim about its fail-closed behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: A baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off.
claims.why: The `freshness` field is a plain dict with no blocking logic in this dataclass; the comment explicitly says it is 'Reported, never blocking'.

observations.what: The `scan` function's docstring claims purity, and the code indeed has no side effects in this chunk; however, it calls `repo_state(root, probe_dirty=probe_dirty)` which may read the filesystem or git, but that is still read-only and not a write, clock, or network operation.

In `parse_acceptances`, the `who` field is parsed but not validated; the docstring says 'anything we cannot fully validate is kept', but missing `who` does not produce a problem, which is consistent with `who` being optional (default empty string).

The `Acceptance.expired` method returns `True` on a `ValueError` from `date.fromisoformat`, which means malformed dates are treated as expired. This aligns with the fail-closed philosophy but could be surprising; it is not contradicted by any docstring in this chunk.

The `DriftItem.blocking` property checks `kind in NON_BLOCKING_KINDS` first, then returns `not self.accepted`. This means an accepted item in a non-blocking kind is still non-blocking, which is consistent with the stated intent but the comment in the code does not elaborate.

risks: scan docstring purity claim | low | The docstring says 'no writes, no clock, no network' but `repo_state` may read git state; if that involves a subprocess or network, the claim could be violated. Verify `repo_state` in this file.

parse_acceptances 'fail closed' | low | The function drops non-list input entirely (returns empty list), which could be seen as failing open if the caller expects a list. The docstring does not specify behavior for non-list input; verify intended behavior.
